active.body:
The most recent Rubin data `tocsin` has reached is MJD 61235.42, which is 54.4 days behind now. The broker mirror normally lags ~16 days; the limit here is 30.

The channel itself is fine — it is running on schedule and committing results. What has stopped is the DATA. A screen re-reading the same frontier every night produces a clean null indefinitely and looks healthy from every other angle, which is why this check exists separately from the staleness check.

Check whether ALeRCE is still ingesting the LSST alert stream before reading any recent null from this channel.

**Cause established 2026-09-05 by `rubin-outage`: SKY_STOPPED.** Independent brokers stop on the same night (ALeRCE 2026-07-14; fink 2026-07-14), so the alert stream itself stopped and no change to the broker path recovers data that was never taken. Do not relax the threshold on this — the condition is real. See `docs/rubin-outage.md`. ZTF, the other public wide-field alert stream, is LIVE (newest night 2026-09-04 via alerce_ztf), so `tocsin-altfeeds` has a current feed to lean on.

`tocsin` has reported the same newest epoch, MJD 61235.41918, on every run since 2026-07-30T10:26:40Z — 38.4 days, against a limit of 7. Source: `results/tocsin/summary.json` → `broker_frontier_mjd`.

The frontier has not yet been observed to advance at all, so there is no measured cadence to compare this against.

The channel is running and committing normally; what has stopped is the mirror. Every null it reports while this holds means *no new sky*, not *clean sky*, and the two are not the same result.

Check whether ALeRCE is still ingesting the LSST alert stream. If the pause turns out to be ordinary batching, raise `FRONTIER_STALL_DAYS` using the cadence recorded in `results/alerts/frontier.json` rather than by guessing again.

The `asassn` adapter reached its service but has no usable path to a light curve.

Reason recorded by the probe: no cone request was accepted (every variant and format in the matrix above), and the vendor client cannot be imported here -- so there is no path to a light curve, only to metadata

A screen over this feed would run, commit and report nothing found -- which is indistinguishable from a quiet sky and is not a result. Read `results/tocsin_altfeeds/probe.json`; the request matrix there records verbatim what the service answered.
